approachQuestion.prompt:
Largest Change Between Readings

A sensor records integer readings in the order they were taken. Return the greatest absolute difference between two consecutive readings.

Limits: 2 ≤ n = readings.length ≤ 200,000; −1,000,000,000 ≤ readings[i] ≤ 1,000,000,000.

Example 1: readings = [11, 7, 9, 2, 8] → 7 (between 9 and 2).
Example 2: readings = [5, 5] → 0.
constraints: The readings are ordered by time; do not change their order.
Return one number: the greatest absolute difference between two consecutive readings.
Do not modify the input array.
Use signed integers at least 32 bits wide; the greatest possible absolute difference is 2,000,000,000 and fits in that range.

options.text: Scan consecutive pairs, calculate each absolute difference, and keep the greatest one found so far.
options.feedback: The original order gives meaning to which readings are consecutive. The current pair and the greatest difference found so far are enough.

options.text: Store the differences for all consecutive pairs in a new array, then find its maximum.
options.feedback: This compares the correct pairs and returns the right result for every allowed input. The extra array stores values you do not need to keep; you can update the maximum during the same scan.

options.text: Sort a copy of the readings and compare consecutive values in the sorted copy.
options.feedback: Sorting loses the original time adjacency. For [4, 1, 7], the required answer is 6, while the largest difference between sorted neighbors is 3.

options.text: Find the minimum and maximum readings, then return their difference.
options.feedback: The extreme readings do not have to be consecutive. For [4, 7, 10], the answer is 3, while the difference between the extremes is 6.

feedback.reason: Choose a method that returns the required value while respecting which readings were consecutive in time. After you submit, you will see how your method is graded; after the second question, you will get the full cost explanation.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “One Running Maximum,” choose one pair: time and auxiliary space. Auxiliary space includes helper variables but excludes the input and the single returned value.
constraints: The readings are ordered by time; do not change their order.
Return one number: the greatest absolute difference between two consecutive readings.
Do not modify the input array.
Use signed integers at least 32 bits wide; the greatest possible absolute difference is 2,000,000,000 and fits in that range.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: We inspect n−1 pairs, using a fixed number of operations for each pair. We keep only the current index and the greatest difference found so far. We do not build an array of differences, so auxiliary space does not grow with the input.
details: linear-constant: the tight pair for one scan and one running maximum.
linear-array: this describes storing every difference, not the method being analyzed.
sort-copy: this describes sorting and copying, which the analyzed method does not use.
constant: this ignores the need to inspect consecutive pairs.
Learning objective: Distinguish adjacency in the original time order from global minimum and maximum values.

methodReveal.title: One Running Maximum
methodReveal.description: Compare each consecutive pair in the original order and update the greatest difference found so far. Keep that maximum as you continue through the readings.
